Bereznehuvate Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mykolaiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. The Jewish farm colony of Nahartav (later Bereznehuvate) was settled in three waves: the first 20 families arrived between 1807 and 1809, joined by a larger second wave in 1815, while a third wave founded the separate colony of Maly Nahartav in 1811. By 1847, Velykyy Nahartav served as the administrative center for the Jewish agricultural colonies of the Kherson province; the Jewish population reached 1,571 (92 percent) by 1897, and a two-story synagogue was built in 1912. The community survived pogroms in both 1918 (organized by Directorate forces) and 1919 (by the Volunteer Army), receiving relief assistance from the ARA, the JDC, and material support from J.I. Shneerson, likely connected to the prominent Chabad Schneerson family documented at Nizhyn and Hadyach elsewhere in this collection. On September 14, 1941, German troops executed 112 Jews; more than 2,000 Jews were murdered across the wider region.
